messages:
alex_dev: Heads-up — BigBank asked for a permanent per-org routing override to route all traffic to a dedicated pool. They said it must survive restarts and not be TTL-limited. :grimacing:

maya_prod: ugh, we usually force an expiry on ad-hoc overrides to avoid cruft. what's the business ask? permanent because of compliance or perf?

alex_dev: it's a mix — they want isolation guarantees for certain endpoints for audits. They also asked we avoid any accidental fallbacks during incidents.

chris_sre: permanent smells bad from an ops/availability POV. If someone pins a route forever it can block autoscaling, capacity rebalancing, and make rollbacks painful. We need audit trail + automatic expiry default.

jonah_platform: can we have a graduated model: default TTL (24h/7d?) + an "enterprise exception" checkbox that requires a signed approval and creates a longer TTL (30d) and a manual permanent opt-in gated behind a PoA? console would show status and owner.

emily_pm: +1 for gating. product wise we can't make permanent the default. also need metrics: number of active overrides, age distribution, and a list in console for easy cleanup.

chris_sre: telemetry gap: we don't currently emit a metric for "override_age_seconds" or an event when an override expires. Right now audit logs have creation but not expiry. Hard to alert on orphaned pins.

alex_dev: noted. also need to clarify semantics for header-based overrides. currently we accept X-Redwood-Org-Route and X-Redwood-Override-Reason headers. how do they interact with TTLs?

maya_prod: header flow today just creates a transient sticky route at runtime; it doesn't write to persistent override store unless the console API is used. customers asked for an API path to create persistent overrides via header for automation.

chris_sre: that would be a security vector. if we allow headers to create persistent state, we must require HMAC signing + admin scope and record actor. Suggest: only allow headers to create ephemeral runtime pins; persistent override API requires OAuth with org.admin scope + signed audit note.

alex_dev: makes sense. example header we can accept for ephemeral runtime pin:

```
X-Redwood-Org: bigbank
X-Redwood-Route: pool-dedicated-eu
X-Redwood-Override-Expiry: 3600  # seconds
```

jonah_platform: for the console UX I'd add a compact pill showing TTL with a countdown and a "renew" button that opens a modal with reason + approver. Also add filters for >30d and sort by age.

emily_pm: action items: 1) decide default TTL (proposal: 7d), 2) require signed approval for >30d, 3) implement metrics + alerts for orphaned overrides, 4) block header->persistent creation.

chris_sre: I'll draft the metrics plan. Quick query we can use to find long-lived overrides (example for events in ClickHouse/BigQuery):

```sql
-- find overrides older than 30 days
SELECT org_id, override_id, MIN(created_at) AS created_at, COUNT(*) AS touch_count
FROM overrides_events
WHERE created_at < TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
GROUP BY org_id, override_id
ORDER BY created_at ASC
LIMIT 200
```

jonah_platform: I'll mock the console pill + renew modal. Will the renew button extend TTL or create a new override?

alex_dev: renew should extend TTL and append an audit note with who renewed and why. Also incremental versioning of overrides so we can rollback to previous routing state.

chris_sre: alert proposal: create an alert when (count_overrides_age_>_30d > 5) per org for non-enterprise-exceptions. Also add a dashboard panel for override churn (created/expired) and per-org active pins.

emily_pm: legal/compliance want to see permanent exceptions in audits. So even for permanent opt-ins we must keep a signed approval doc and a pointer to the approval in the override record.

alex_dev: ok. security note: enforce RBAC so only org admins and SREs (for emergency) can create >30d. For emergency breakglass we can allow temporary bypass but it must emit a high-severity audit event and auto-expire in 1 hour unless manually extended.

maya_prod: suggestion: when an override is active, route preferences should still respect capacity-based fallback. We need a config flag on override "hard_pin": true/false. Hard_pin = true forces no fallback — must be explicit and requires exec approval. Default false (soft pin).

chris_sre: hard_pin true is scary. If set, we must have circuit-breaker limits and quota checks. Also forbid hard_pin for multi-region pools that don't have capacity guarantees.

alex_dev: agree. we'll add validation in the API: reject hard_pin if pool_capacity_reserved = false.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: policy-service v2.7 deployed to staging at 2026-02-12T09:12:34Z - includes endpoint /overrides and TTL field. :rocket:

emily_pm: nice. next steps: alex draft RFC with API shape + RBAC + audit pointers, chris to add metrics + alert query, jonah to prototype console UX. we'll sync next Tue 10am.

alex_dev: assigning: @chris_sre for metrics, @jonah_platform for UI, @alex_dev to write RFC. ping me if you need diffs for policy-service. :thumbsup:
